newsitem.title: JAPAN: No accord with China to shelve isles dispute-Japan.
newsitem.headline: No accord with China to shelve isles dispute-Japan.

text.p: Japan on Monday denied that agreement had been reached with China to shelve a row over a chain of islands in the East China Sea, contradicting remarks by China's foreign minister.

"China says it wants to shelve the matter because its position is different from Japan's," said Vice Foreign Minister Sadayuki Hayashi. "But there has been no accord between the two countries to set it aside," he told a news conference.

The comments were in response to remarks by Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen who told Japanese reporters in Beijing that Tokyo and Beijing had agreed to set aside the sovereignty dispute over what Japan claims as the Senkaku islands and China and Taiwan call the Diaoyu islands.
"Our stance on the ownership of the Senkaku Islands has been consistent: they are an integral part of Japanese territory," Hayashi said.

Japan's claim to the uninhabited islands has triggered anti-Japanese demonstrations in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse on one of the islands in July.
Emotions were fanned last month when a Hong Kong activist drowned after he jumped into stormy waters around the island to demonstrate Chinese claims.
On Saturday, Japan's top government spokesman said Tokyo may send two special envoys to Beijing after general elections on October 20 to negotiate an end to the row.
"We have to clear up any doubts they (China) have about Japan," Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters. "We have to seek a compromise."
